topLine: NSW's budget outlook dominated the day, with Treasurer Daniel Mookhey flagging a further write-down of stamp duty and land tax revenue that the Sydney Morning Herald reports could reach $16 billion, and the AFR reporting the revenue hit will cost the state its surplus next year. Labor also put a $6.8 billion South Coast rail package on the table for the March election, while the Auditor-General reported "significant deficiencies" in Powerhouse Museum contracts. With the state poll now under four months away, commentators are reading the Victorian campaign and One Nation's rise for signals about NSW.

briefing.topLine: NSW's budget outlook dominated the day, with Treasurer Daniel Mookhey flagging a further write-down of stamp duty and land tax revenue that the Sydney Morning Herald reports could reach $16 billion, and the AFR reporting the revenue hit will cost the state its surplus next year. Labor also put a $6.8 billion South Coast rail package on the table for the March election, while the Auditor-General reported "significant deficiencies" in Powerhouse Museum contracts. With the state poll now under four months away, commentators are reading the Victorian campaign and One Nation's rise for signals about NSW.
briefing.localWatch: Labor's $6.8 billion South Coast rail pledge, which the Illawarra Mercury reports would extend passing loops to allow longer freight trains if the party wins in March, is the clearest regional offer so far. Locally, Kiama's mayor has used a council update to push back on state government planning, and a new short-stay surgery service at Shellharbour Hospital is aimed at cutting elective surgery waits across the region.

stories.headline: Longer freight trains are part of 'critical' South Coast rail upgrade
stories.summary: The Illawarra Mercury reports that Labor's $6.8 billion South Coast rail package would extend passing loops so longer freight trains can run on the line. The commitment is conditional on the party winning the March state election.

stories.headline: Mayor’s update: State Government can't turn Kiama into Gold Coast
stories.summary: Kiama Council has published a mayoral update headlined with the message that the state government cannot turn Kiama into the Gold Coast. Only the headline was available, so no further detail of the mayor's remarks is reported here.

stories.headline: Shellharbour Hospital's plan to fast-track surgeries and ease region waitlist times
stories.summary: A high-volume short-stay surgery service has begun at Shellharbour Hospital, the Illawarra Mercury reports, introduced under a NSW government plan to cut elective surgery waiting lists. The paper reports it is intended to ease waiting times across the region.

stories.headline: 'Everyone got done': Four smoke shops shut in Illawarra vape blitz
stories.summary: NSW Health has closed four Illawarra tobacconists over alleged sales of illegal tobacco and vapes, according to the South Coast Register. The paper reports the health minister warned of further action if such sales continue.

stories.headline: 'Get it right': The Groundz call on the Dapto school site plans
stories.summary: The Groundz chief executive Katrina Novak has called for earlier consultation on apartment plans for the former Dapto school site, the Illawarra Mercury reports. The Housing Trust says it has passed the feedback on to its architects.

stories.headline: NSW Labor is ‘trampling over party principles’ with preselections by captain’s call, members say
stories.summary: The Guardian reports that NSW Labor members say the use of captain's picks for preselections is trampling over party principles. Only the headline was supplied, so the specific seats and members involved are not detailed here.

stories.headline: Exclusive poll: Jim’s got us in a state of despair
stories.summary: The Daily Telegraph reports an exclusive poll finding almost six in 10 NSW residents expect the economy to worsen, amid what the paper describes as recession fears. No further polling detail was supplied.

stories.headline: ‘Absolute Furious’ – Kellie Sloane says Minns Government not standing up to youth crime
stories.summary: 2GB reports that NSW Opposition Leader Kellie Sloane has criticised the Minns government over youth crime, describing the situation as out of control following an attack in the Sydney CBD.

stories.headline: Stamp duty freefall could cost NSW budget $16 billion
stories.summary: Treasurer Daniel Mookhey says a volatile property market will force a further write-down of stamp duty and land tax revenue, which the Sydney Morning Herald reports could cost the budget $16 billion. The AFR reports falling house prices have wiped about 3 per cent off state revenue and will cost NSW its surplus next year, with the treasurer attributing the hit to interest rate rises and tax changes. A separate Herald report puts $8 billion of lost revenue down in part to changes made in the federal budget.

stories.headline: Minns Labor Government invests in grassroots rugby
stories.summary: The NSW government says a further $2.18 million has been awarded to clubs, associations and councils in round two of the NSW Rugby World Cup Legacy Program, part of a $10 million commitment to grow rugby union across the state.

stories.headline: Auditor-General blasts ‘significant deficiencies’ in Powerhouse Museum contracts in damning report
stories.summary: The Sydney Morning Herald reports the Auditor-General has found "significant deficiencies" in contracting for the Powerhouse Museum. The paper says the findings add to pressure on the billion-dollar project, which opened earlier this month.

stories.headline: Electoral finance reform, déjà vu without the safeguards
stories.summary: The Mandarin has published a piece on electoral finance reform, arguing in its headline that the changes echo earlier reforms but lack the safeguards. Only the headline was supplied, so the detail of its argument is not reported here.

stories.headline: Anger, uncertainty and ‘deals with the devil’: Countdown on to an election like no other
stories.summary: The Herald reports that political operatives are setting aside their past assumptions about NSW elections as the March poll approaches, describing a contest shaped by anger and uncertainty.

stories.headline: One Nation’s result in Victoria could terrify both NSW leaders
stories.summary: The Daily Telegraph argues that a surge in the One Nation vote at the Victorian election should serve as a warning for both Labor and the Coalition in NSW. Only the headline was supplied.

stories.headline: Tanking housing adds to reasons Minns has to go it alone
stories.summary: The Australian argues that a weakening housing market adds to the case for Chris Minns to run a presidential-style re-election bid that distances NSW Labor from Anthony Albanese's federal government.

stories.headline: Premiers and Opposition Leaders who’ve Lost their Seats – the Gurgle Hole of History
stories.summary: Antony Green has updated his 2021 list of premiers and opposition leaders who have lost their own seats at elections, adding five new names including Peter Dutton, who lost Dickson at the 2025 federal election.

stories.headline: Tough talk isn’t enough: Minns must act on youth bail laws, Hadley
stories.summary: In the Daily Telegraph, Ray Hadley argues that Premier Chris Minns needs to act on youth bail laws rather than rely on tough rhetoric. Only the headline was supplied.

elsewhere.text: A veteran Nationals figure is proposing a $500,000 penalty on MPs who defect from the party, the Herald reports, as the Nationals try to stem losses to One Nation and the crossbench.
Ben Raue examines what the final polls, including a News Corp-commissioned YouGov MRP, suggest about the shape of the Victorian race.
The Guardian summarises the major parties' promises on cost of living, health, transport and crime ahead of the Victorian state election.
Victoria's party leaders answer Crikey's questions on debt, crime and taxes on the eve of the state election.
Final results from New Zealand's 7 November election have produced a parliament with no party holding a majority.
The Australian reports a poll showing the Albanese government at a new low as voters worry about an economic downturn.
